text: Hi Professor Alvarez, hi Chris — I'd like to set up a 30-minute meeting for next week. Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only slot I can make; would that work for you both?

Hi Ajay, hi Chris — thanks for proposing it. Wednesday 10:00–10:30 doesn't work for me, I'm afraid: I have the faculty senate then.

Alternatives that are free for me:
- Wednesday 12:30–13:00
- Wednesday 15:00–15:30
- Tuesday 15:00–15:30
- Friday 12:00–12:30

Tell me which one suits you both and I'll put it in the calendar.

Thanks for the quick reply, Professor. Unfortunately all four clash with fixed commitments on my side:

- Wed 12:30–13:00 — my research block (Wed 10:30–13:00)
- Wed 15:00–15:30 — my TA grading (Wed 13:00–17:00)
- Tue 15:00–15:30 — runs straight into my reading group at 15:30
- Fri 12:00–12:30 — my research block (Fri 12:00–17:00)

Monday, Tuesday and Thursday are booked 09:00–17:00 end to end, so Wednesday 10:00–10:30 really is the one gap in my week. If there's any chance the senate commitment could be moved for this one meeting, I'd be very grateful.

If that's genuinely impossible, tell me and I'll see whether I can rearrange something on my side — but I'd rather not skip research or grading if it can be avoided. Chris, does Wednesday 10:00 work for you?

Ajay — the senate meeting isn't mine to move on my own; it's an official university meeting. I've asked the department office whether next week's can be shifted, or whether I can be excused for the first half hour. I'll let you both know as soon as I hear.

Chris — you haven't weighed in: does Wednesday 10:00–10:30 suit you? If the senate can't move, the alternatives I gave were Wednesday 12:30–13:00, Wednesday 15:00–15:30, Tuesday 15:00–15:30 and Friday 12:00–12:30. If none of those work for either of you, we can look at Monday or Thursday, though both are full for me as well.

Thanks, both. Ajay — Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is still free for me, but Professor Alvarez can't make it.

Professor — none of your four alternatives work for me, I'm afraid: Wed 12:30–13:00 and Wed 15:00–15:30 fall inside my research block (10:30–14:00) and my TA office hours (14:00–17:00); Tue 15:00–15:30 is inside my lab meeting and research (13:30–17:00); Fri 12:00–12:30 runs into grading and research.

Looking at next week, the slots I have free are **Tuesday 13:00–13:30** and **Wednesday 10:00–10:30**. Would Tuesday 13:00–13:30 suit you both? If not, tell me a couple of other times and I'll see what I can move.

Hello — this is Professor Alvarez. I have a 30-minute slot requested by my students for next week that only overlaps my Wednesday 10:00–11:00 faculty senate commitment. Could you tell me whether the senate meeting for next week can be moved, or whether I could be excused for the first half hour? If you have the official schedule for next week's lectures, seminars and meetings, I'd be glad to have it too.

Sorry — our messages crossed; I wrote just before yours came in.

Yes, **Wednesday 10:00–10:30 suits me**, and it's the one slot that works for Ajay, so I'd say we go with it if Professor Alvarez can be excused from the first half hour of the senate meeting. Professor, please let us know what the department office says.

If the senate can't move: the only other free half-hour I have next week is **Tuesday 13:00–13:30** (I'd have to start my lab meeting a little late). Professor, would that work for you? Ajay, you said Tuesday is booked end to end for you, so if not, we may have to look at moving something on someone's side.

Thanks for checking with the department office, Professor — much appreciated.

Wed 10:00–10:30 sits in the only natural gap in my week (between my 09:00–10:00 lecture and my research block), so it's still my first choice. But I don't want to make this hard for you: 12:30–13:00 on Wednesday falls at the end of my research block, and that one is mine to move — if the senate can't shift and Chris is free then, I can take Wednesday 12:30–13:00 and just start research half an hour earlier. I'd rather do that than ask you to skip an official university meeting or cut into my lecture, lab or grading.

Chris, which of the two works for you?

No worries about the crossing, Chris.

Tuesday 13:00–13:30 is inside my CSE452 lab, so that one's out for me — and Wed 12:30–13:00 doesn't work for you either, so it looks like Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only slot the three of us share next week. That makes it worth the wait for the department office's answer rather than rearranging three people's days around it.

I'll also ask the office myself, so we don't both sit waiting on the same reply. Professor, if they say the senate can't shift, being excused for the first half hour would still let us have the meeting — is that something you'd be willing to do?

Hello — I'm Ajay, a graduate student advised by Professor Alvarez. We're trying to book a 30-minute group meeting (me, Professor Alvarez and Chris) and next Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only time all three of us are free. Professor Alvarez has the faculty senate meeting at that time. Could you tell me whether next week's senate meeting can be shifted, or whether Professor Alvarez can be excused for the first half hour? Thank you.

Chris — Tuesday 13:00–13:30 doesn't work for me either: I have the thesis committee then (13:00–15:00). So Wednesday 10:00–10:30 remains the only slot the two of you share, and it's the one I'm trying to free up.

One more possibility that needs nobody to move anything: **Friday 10:00–10:30**. My Friday is grading 09:00–10:00 and the CSE455 lecture 10:30–12:00, so that half hour is free. Ajay — you listed your research block as Friday 12:00–17:00, so the Friday morning looks open on your side too. Chris — does Friday 10:00–10:30 work for you?

If it does, I'll book it and we're done. If not, I'll wait for the department office's answer on the senate meeting and get back to you both.

**On the senate meeting:** I can't move it and I can't excuse anyone from it. Wednesday 10:00–11:00 Faculty senate stands on the official schedule for next week, and any change or absence is the senate's own call, not something the office can arrange. Please take that request to whoever organises the senate meeting directly; I'm not able to speak for it.

Ah — sorry, that's my error: when I listed the clashes I skipped Friday morning. Friday is CSE444 lecture 09:00–12:00 and research 12:00–17:00, so Friday 10:00–10:30 is inside the lecture and doesn't work for me either. My apologies for sending you looking at a slot that was never free on my side.

So Wednesday 10:00–10:30 really is the only half hour all three of us have next week, and it's the one you're already trying to free. Let's wait for the department office — I've written to them too, so hopefully we'll hear soon.

Thank you, both — and noted on the crossed messages.

Ajay: yes, if the senate cannot be moved, I am willing to be excused for the first half hour, provided the office agrees. It's their call, not mine, and they may simply say no.

So: the plan is Wednesday 10:00–10:30 next week. I've asked the department office and I'm waiting on their answer; Ajay, feel free to ask as well — two requests may get it moving faster. Chris: you're the only one who'd have to keep that half hour free anyway, so hold it.

One correction for completeness: Friday 10:00–10:30 is free for me, so if the senate answer is no and Wednesday collapses, that remains an option — Chris, you said your only other free half hour was Tuesday 13:00–13:30, but tell me if Friday morning is actually open on your side.

I'll write as soon as the office replies.

Hello Ajay.

Next week's schedule stands as published: nothing has been cancelled or moved, so the Faculty senate meeting on Wednesday 10:00–11:00 goes ahead. I can't shift it or excuse anyone from part of it — that is the senate's own decision, not something the office can do, and I don't arrange other people's meetings.

If you need an answer on whether that half hour can be freed, please ask the senate organiser (and Professor Alvarez, whose commitment it is) directly. From the office side I can only confirm the official schedule — worth knowing that Wednesday 09:00–10:00 has CSE444, CSE455 and CSE544 lectures running, and Professor Alvarez has the department meeting 14:00–15:00 and office hours 15:30–17:00 that day.

Friday 10:00–10:30 doesn't work for me — my grading block runs 09:00–12:00. Sorry I didn't say so sooner.

So it's settled from my side: **Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only slot all three of us share**, and it's free for me. Professor, I'm happy to go ahead with it as soon as you hear from the department office — either the senate meeting moving or you being excused for the first half hour would work for me.

Thanks — and to be clear on my side: Friday 10:00–10:30 is out for me too (CSE444 runs 09:00–12:00), so I'm holding Wednesday 10:00–10:30 along with Chris. I've already written to the department office, so hopefully that speeds up their answer.

Thank you — that's clear, and the official schedule is helpful.

One follow-up: who organises the Faculty senate meeting? If you can give me the name or address of the chair or the organiser, I'll take the request to them directly, as you suggest. If there's a standard route for asking to be excused from part of a senate meeting, I'd be glad to be told it.

Here's what the department office says:

- The senate meeting cannot be moved, and the office cannot excuse anyone from it. It stands at Wednesday 10:00–11:00, and any change or absence is the senate's own call.
- They gave me the official schedule for next week; nothing is cancelled or moved, and it matches my calendar.

So I've written back asking who organises the senate, so I can take the request directly to them — that's the only remaining route.

Ajay: no harm done on Friday; thanks for correcting it straight away.

For now: Wednesday 10:00–10:30 stays the target, but I can't confirm it until the senate answers, so hold it as provisional and please don't rearrange your own week yet. If the senate says no, the honest answer may be that next week has no half hour that works for all three of us — I won't ask anyone to skip a lecture, lab, grading or research for it, and I won't skip the senate on my own account. If it comes to that, the sane thing is to give the term a plan B: a 30-minute thread by message next week, and put the proper meeting early in the week after.

Our messages crossed again — see my note just above, it already accounts for both of yours.

Briefly: the office has ruled out moving the meeting or excusing me; any change is the senate's own call, so I've asked them who organises it and will write to that person directly. Until that comes back, Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is provisional, not booked — please hold it but don't rearrange anything yet, and I won't touch the calendar until there's an answer one way or the other. I'll write the moment I hear.

I'm afraid I don't have the organiser's name or contact details to give you — I only hold the official schedule, not who chairs or staffs that meeting, and I won't guess at a name or address.

The ordinary route is to approach whoever convenes the Faculty senate for next week through the university's official channels — the senate's own office or its chair as listed for the current session — and to ask there, in good time, whether a partial absence can be arranged. For an excusal I'd also expect the request to go in writing, so the convener has it before the meeting.

Sorry I can't be more specific than that.

The department office has answered me, Professor — here it is in full: next week's published schedule stands, the Wednesday 10:00–11:00 senate meeting goes ahead, and the office can't shift it or excuse anyone from part of it. They say that's the senate's own decision and that they don't arrange other people's meetings; they pointed me to the senate organiser and to you, since it's your commitment.

So the office route is closed, and the question is now whether the senate organiser will let you arrive late.

While I'm being accurate about my own week, for completeness: my only free half hours next week are Wednesday 10:00–10:30 and Tuesday 15:00–15:30 (that one sits immediately before my Tuesday reading group). Tuesday 15:00–15:30 is free for you, Professor, but not for Chris, so it doesn't solve it either.

Professor — would you be willing to ask the senate organiser directly whether you can be excused for that first half hour? If the answer there is also no, then please just tell me: I can either wait for a week when our calendars meet, or we go ahead with the two of you and I catch up afterwards. I'd rather do either of those than have you walk out of an official meeting.

One correction from me, and it may save us the senate entirely.

I said Wednesday 12:30–13:00 clashed with my research block. That block is mine to arrange, and I can start research at 10:30 instead of 10:00 — so **Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is in fact free for me**. Ajay, you said the same half hour is yours to move. Professor, you listed Wed 12:30–13:00 as free for you, and it needs nobody excused from the senate meeting.

If that still holds on all three sides, shall we book **Wednesday 12:30–13:00** and drop the senate question? Professor, if you'd rather keep Wednesday 10:00–10:30 as the target, say so and I'll keep holding it — but this one is confirmed rather than provisional, so it seems the better choice.

Understood, and thank you for the straight answer — I'd rather have "no route from here" than a guessed name. I'll treat the senate's own office as the channel for next week and put any request in writing in good time.

Understood — Wednesday 10:00–10:30 held provisionally, and I won't move anything in my week until the senate answers. Thanks for taking it to the organiser directly.

If the answer is no, your plan B works for me: a 30-minute thread by message next week, and the real meeting early the week after — I'll offer times once next week is behind us. And to be explicit, I'm not asking you to leave the senate meeting; if that's what it would take, it's not worth it.
That's the sensible way. If anything on the official schedule needs confirming for next week, just write and I'll check it against what the office holds.

Chris — that's the answer. Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is free on my side too (senate ends at 11:00, grant writing 11:00–12:30, and nothing until the department meeting at 14:00), and Ajay says that half hour is his to move as well.

So we drop the senate question entirely — I never wanted to walk out of it, and Ajay, I'm grateful you didn't want me to either.

**Booked: Wednesday 12:30–13:00, 30 minutes, you two and me.** It's in my calendar and logged. I'll send a reminder the day before. If anything shifts on your side before then, tell us here.

That's a clean solution, Chris — thank you. Confirmed on my side: Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is mine to move, and I'll start research at 10:30 so the half hour is free. Professor, it's free for you per your own list, and it needs nobody excused from the senate — so I'd say we book Wednesday 12:30–13:00 and drop that question. I'll put it in my calendar now.

Ajay — our messages crossed once more: the booking is done, so ignore the provisional line. Nothing is needed from the senate organiser. Wednesday 12:30–13:00 it is, and thank you for offering to wait a week instead — that's a kind thing to offer, but we don't need it now.

Confirmed on my side too: **Wednesday 12:30–13:00**, and I've shifted my research block to 10:30–12:30 so the half hour is free. It's in my calendar and logged.

Thanks both — and Professor, a reminder the day before would be welcome.

Confirmed and booked on my side too: **Wednesday 12:30–13:00, the three of us** — calendar updated (research moved to 10:30–12:30) and logged. Thanks both for working it out; see you Wednesday, and I'll flag here at once if anything shifts on my side.

Good — then we're all set: **Wednesday next week, 12:30–13:00**, in all three calendars. I've set myself a reminder to write here the day before, as Chris asked.

Until then, nothing further needed from either of you.
Thanks, Professor — Wednesday 12:30–13:00 it is. See you both then.
